title: My First SaaS Project Just Hit $11K/Month
promo_conflict: Guest is promoting his own product (Vogola) and his growth playbook. Starter Story makes money from sponsors, and a sponsor read for a customer-data tool was cut out around L0038-L0042. Revenue is backed by a Stripe dashboard shown on screen, but signup numbers are vague ('a few 10,000 signups').

idea.name: Vogola – AI video clipping/editing SaaS
idea.one_liner: Web app that turns long-form videos (e.g. pasted YouTube links) into short vertical clips with captions, sold as a monthly subscription to clippers, creators, agencies and long-form brands.
idea.customer: Clippers, content creators, agencies and long-form content brands (B2C/prosumer)
idea.offer: AI agent that clips long-form content into short clips with caption styles and aspect ratios, plus a beta full video editor
idea.revenue_model: Recurring SaaS subscription (MRR); price per plan not stated

key_quotes.quote: So Vogola is basically an AI video editing agent that can turn any piece of content into like viral edited nice clips.
my target like customer and ICP is basically clippers, content creators, agencies, and longform brands.
since there's already a proven market out there video editing clipping, I'm like, why not me just build another clipping tool?
Basically, I was leveraging already viral proven like formats and like topics.
basically, I just micro analyzed and copied their entire format to the T and I just change and iterated from my own product.
It's like a clipping tool and an AI clipper just combining to one.

claims.quote: I've built an AI app called Vogola that makes me over $10,000 every single month without any coding experience.

claims.claim: About $11,200 MRR generated in the last four weeks
claims.quote: In the last four weeks alone, we have generated about $11,200 a monthly recurring revenue.

claims.claim: Roughly 10,000+ signups and about 400 paying users
claims.quote: we have roughly gone over like a few 10,000 signups and we have about 400 paying users.

claims.claim: Four months to build; started marketing about 5-6 months ago
claims.quote: I spent four months building it and then I just started working it about, let's say five to six months ago.

claims.claim: First $2-3k MRR came from Twitter/X alone
claims.quote: That was our first like zero to like two thousand three thousand dollars in monthly recurring revenue that was purely just off Twitter.

claims.quote: And all it takes is going to be like 45 minutes like a day.

claims.quote: We're already at 10.8k followers, just a brand new UGC account.
This video got 132,000 views, 18,000 views, 21,000 views.

claims.claim: Only marketing cost is a ManyChat subscription at $15/month
claims.quote: The only thing that costs you this many chapters of subscription for $15 a month, this is all you need to cross $10,000 a month.

acquisition_channels.details: Built a personal brand on X/Twitter and rode viral AI trends, e.g. an OpenClaw plugin/video tied to Vogola. This took it to $2-3k MRR.
New Instagram UGC account. He copied competitors' viral formats (hook, audio, text, demo length, CTA), filmed his own face and posted 3-6 times a day, about 45 minutes daily.
ManyChat ($15/month) connected to Instagram to auto-reply to people who engage with posts (inbound/opt-in, not cold DMs).

ideas.delivery: Self-serve web app. The user pastes a YouTube link and picks caption style and aspect ratio (e.g. 9:16), and the AI generates clips; a beta in-app editor is also offered. Built and run solo by the founder with vibe-coding tools (Lovable, then Claude, now Codex) on Supabase, Vercel, Cloudflare and AWS rendering.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Users upload or link personal data, so UK GDPR applies to user data and analytics (PostHog/DataFast cookies need PECR cookie consent). DMCC Act 2024 subscription-contract rules (clear pre-contract info, reminders, easy cancellation) apply to consumer subscriptions. Clipping third-party YouTube content raises copyright (CDPA 1988) and platform-terms risk for users.
